summary: The dnf module installs, upgrades, removes and lists packages and groups. Pass lists to name instead of looping; removing groups installed by Ansible may fail; the yum backend was removed in 2.17.
questions: How do I install packages on RHEL/Fedora with Ansible?
Why can't Ansible remove a package group it installed?
Can I still use the yum backend with ansible.builtin.dnf?
Should I loop over packages with dnf?

answer_card.title: dnf module overview
answer_card.answer_md:
`ansible.builtin.dnf` manages packages and groups with dnf.
- Pass a **list to `name`** instead of `loop:` for efficiency.
- Removing groups installed by Ansible can fail (dnf API doesn't mark them installed).
- `use_backend=yum` / `ansible.builtin.yum` exist for syntax only; the YUM backend was removed in 2.17.
